reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes a slip mode transition from screw to edge dislocations and a resulting strength plateau in HfMoNbTaW and Hf0.5MoNbTaW, but these alloys are fundamentally different from TiVNbTa (e.g., they contain W and Hf, not Ti and V). The hypothesis extrapolates this mechanism to a Mo-doped TiVNbTa system without direct evidence that Mo alone, in a TiVNbTa matrix, will produce the same dislocation behavior or strength enhancement. The claim about thermal conductivity is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mo addition to TiVNbTa enhances solid-solution strengthening.
Mo addition induces a slip mode transition from screw to edge dislocations.
Edge dislocation dominance reduces dislocation mobility and improves high-temperature strength.
The proposed mechanism operates without compromising thermal conductivity.
The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates this mechanism in Mo-containing RHEAs.
